description: Exact approved cryptographic dependency graph for Milestone 4 Part B.
A machine-readable lock over the components that perform cryptography or feed it. Each
entry pins coordinate, role, packaging, expected file name, exact byte size and SHA-256,
so a substituted, truncated, re-versioned or extra component fails verification instead
of being compiled into an APK. tools/verify/security-dependency-lock.mjs enforces the
structure and the resolved graph; the Gradle task :verifySecureDependencyLock enforces
the bytes inside the task graph, before any compiler, test runner, lint analysis, dexer
Not provenance, and not Gradle's global strict dependency verification. The digests were
taken from Maven Central, which is also where Gradle downloads from, so a match proves the
bytes in the build cache are the bytes Maven Central serves -- not that Conscrypt or
Bouncy Castle signed them. There is no gradle/verification-metadata.xml and no whole
repository lock; the remaining AndroidX/Kotlin/Gradle transitives are pinned by

configurations.name: debugAndroidTestRuntimeClasspath
configurations.note: Resolves no crypto component at all. Measured in run 38713963400: the resolved report for this configuration contains zero org.conscrypt or org.bouncycastle modules, even though app reaches transport-lan through implementation (app/build.gradle.kts:170) and app's debugRuntimeClasspath does carry all four production artifacts. This is the AGP split-APK model: debugAndroidTestRuntimeClasspath describes only the instrumentation APK, whose classes run inside the tested app's process, while the production dependencies live in the separately built tested APK. Emptiness is the assertion here, not a skipped check: any crypto component appearing on this configuration fails verification. The tested APK is covered by app:debugRuntimeClasspath at expect full, and the CI evidence step records both the tested APK's packaged native libraries and that assembleDebugAndroidTest builds the tested APK.
